title: E2E Networks Ltd - 544783 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: E2E Networks Q2 FY27 revenue rose 43% QoQ to INR2,238 million, with EBITDA margin at 76.6% and PAT at INR727 million.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR2,238 million, up 411% YoY and 43% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR1,715 million (76.6% margin, up 141 bps QoQ). PAT rose to INR727 million from INR439 million in Q1, with PAT margin at 32.5%. Management attributed the gains to Blackwell GPU contribution, better utilisation and higher average realisation per GPU. Management declined to give guidance, utilisation, contracted-revenue mix or capex timing, and said the next B200 batch was expected to go live this quarter.

segments.name: GPU cloud / Blackwell capacity
segments.commentary: Blackwell GPU contribution and higher average realisation per GPU drove the quarter. The existing B200 batch moved from pay-as-you-go to a multi-year contract of nearly INR1,000 crore running through June 2029, and the flagship Blackwell capacity is fully utilised under that contract.

segments.name: Sovereign AI platform (TIR and Jarvis)
segments.commentary: Management described the platform as the core of future growth and a full-stack offering for training, inference and agentic workloads. Blaze, Endpoint and Jarvis inference products are in soft release, with official launch a few weeks away.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given on MRR, exit rate, capex or utilisation; management said it does not give speculative capex guidance.
Management described the business as a 70%+ EBITDA margin business over the medium to long term, and said it sees no change in that target.
Next B200 batch (about 1,024 GPUs) expected to be deployed this quarter; no contract decided yet for that batch.
For uncontracted or short-term contracted capacity, management expects earnings to grow from the existing asset base.
Order-to-deployment cycle for GPUs is typically 3 to 6 months, per management.
capex_capacity: Next B200 batch of about 1,024 GPUs expected to go live in Q3 FY27 (current quarter); management said it expects deployment this quarter.
No visibility disclosed on B300 or Vera Rubin allotment for FY28-FY29; management will announce once plans are firm.
Management said it is open to debt as long as cash flow supports repayment, with no defined debt ceiling; future equity raise would be announced.
Management said it is open to off-balance-sheet GPU funding and to partnerships such as with L&T, with no specifics.
Some GPUs are used internally for R&D and platform build-out rather than sold.
demand_pricing: INR1,000 crore Blackwell contract with a sovereign AI customer runs through June 2029; it converts existing B200 capacity from pay-as-you-go to multi-year. Management would not say whether MRR is fully baked in, citing usage variability.
Management would not comment on the 85% gross margin reference, saying it is not a quarterly target; Q2 gross margin was about 88% per analyst framing.
Management declined to split revenue by inference, training or storage, and declined to quantify utilisation, citing volatility.
On GPU price increases, management gave no timeline for pass-through to MRR, stating it prioritises customer commitments and that earnings should grow on existing uncontracted assets.

Competition: management said the market is a global TAM of about USD 1 trillion and that there is no direct competition among a few players; it did not directly address domestic scale gaps versus players with large GPU fleets.

qa_highlights.question: When will the next B200 batch go live and when will revenue start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the next B200 lot is expected to go live this quarter, hopefully soon, and it will inform investors when live.

qa_highlights.question: How much of current MRR of about INR75 crore comes from the INR1,000 crore contract, and is MRR fully baked in?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contribution varies with usage but can be approximated from the INR1,000 crore value and contract period; it would not comment on incremental MRR.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the 88% gross margin, and where are operating costs going?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not sure about the 85% reference and reiterated a 70%+ EBITDA margin view for the medium to long term, without a quarterly target.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an MRR exit guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not give guidance and prefers to review past performance.

qa_highlights.question: What is India AI Mission revenue share and renewal pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: India AI customers were roughly 13% to 15% of Q2 revenue; management said it is building relationships beyond that programme.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international revenue mix and contracted revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: International was roughly 20% to 25% of Q2 revenue; management declined to share the contracted vs short-term split, calling it too volatile and with no target set.

qa_highlights.question: What debt levels is management comfortable with, and is there an equity raise under the INR1,500 crore enabling resolution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no defined upper limit on debt, provided front-end cash flow supports repayment and lender covenants are met; it would inform the market of any equity raise.

qa_highlights.question: What is utilisation and how does the TIR platform compare with global cloud offerings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation is a point-in-time metric and that fleet-wide realisation is the better measure; it said platform competitiveness should be judged over the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: How does the Indian competitive landscape, with rivals at about 90,000 and 8,000 GPUs, affect E2E?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it operates in a global market of about USD 1 trillion TAM and that there is enough demand for everyone, without addressing relative scale directly.

qa_highlights.question: Will the economics change when customers move to platform-based (not raw compute) offerings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this would be answered over time and gave no margin, realisation or ROC numbers; it said most GPUs today run on its platforms with very little bare metal sold.

risks_watch: Quarter-on-quarter numbers may be volatile, and the company declined to give utilisation, contracted-revenue mix or segment splits.
Customer concentration risk: the INR1,000 crore contract is a large share of current capacity, and the flagship Blackwell capacity is fully committed under it.
Next B200 batch (about 1,024 GPUs) is due this quarter but has no contract yet; monitor go-live timing and pricing for uncontracted capacity.
Rising GPU prices globally, with no stated timeline for pass-through into MRR or renewals.
Competitive intensity in India, with peers reportedly at larger GPU scale; the company says the market is large enough.
Unclear funding plans for future GPU capex (debt, off-balance-sheet, equity), and no B300 or Vera Rubin visibility for FY28-FY29.
Management time-limited responses on the 85% gross margin reference, leaving sustainability unclear.
summary.management_tone: Confident on reported results and platform strategy, but evasive on forward-looking numbers: management repeatedly declined to give guidance, utilisation, contracted-revenue share, MRR exit rate and capex timing, citing volatility and a 'long-term' focus.
key_quotes: This has been another strong quarter for E2E Networks, where we have continued executing similar to the previous quarter.
we are looking at this as a 70% plus EBITDA margin business. That's what we feel for the medium term and the long term.
We do not give speculative capex guidance.
So we find that this order-to-deployment cycle can vary between 3 to 6 months, typically.
